Remember Laurel versus Yanny, the 2018 audio clip that split the internet into two camps? This video is the Chinese counterpart: the same recording sounds to some listeners like “gulu” and to others like “mimi.”

As Fanyu Meng explains, the difference comes down to how well each listener perceives high frequencies, that is, the upper end of their hearing range and their hearing thresholds there. This varies from person to person, but younger people generally hear high frequencies better, so they are more likely to hear “mimi.”

Shared by Fanyu Meng on Ziyu Acoustics.
